note: bracchia: arms (limbs).

latin: saepe trans finem iaculo nobilis expedito?

note: iaculo nobilis expedito: famous for the javelin thrown.

english: Why does he lie hidden, as of marine
note: marinae agrees with Thetidis.

latin: filium dicunt Thetidis sub lacrimosa Troiae

english: deaths, lest manly

latin: cultus in caedem et Lycias proriperet catervas?

note: cultus: dress, attire; proriperet: hurry (him) forth; 'him' implied.

latin: Vides ut alta stet nive candidum
english: Do you see how, with deep snow, stands gleaming white
note: Question runs to line 4. candidum (line 1) agrees with Soracte (line 2): Soracte stands white with deep snow.

english: Soracte, and no longer they sustain the burden,
note: nec iam sustineant: subjunctive in the indirect question; subject silvae on line 3.

english: the labouring woods, and with frost
the rivers have come to a standstill, sharp?
note: acuto agrees with gelu (line 3): 'with sharp frost'. constiterint: perfect subjunctive, the rivers have stopped (frozen).

english: dissolve the cold, logs upon the hearth
note: dissolve frigus: 'melt away the cold'.

english: generously piling on, and more kindly
draw out the four-year-old, from the Sabine,
note: quadrimum agrees with merum (line 8); Sabina agrees with diota (line 8): 'from the Sabine two-eared jar'.

english: O Thaliarchus, unmixed wine, two-eared jar.
note: Thaliarche: vocative of Thaliarchus. diota: ablative, 'from the two-handled jar' (a Greek word).

english: leave to the gods the rest; who, as soon as
note: simul = simul ac, 'as soon as'.

english: have laid low the winds, on the seething sea
note: stravere: perfect (straverunt).

english: battling it out, neither the cypresses

english: nor the old ash-trees are shaken.

latin: quid sit futurum cras, fuge quaerere et
english: what is going to be tomorrow, flee from asking, and
note: fuge quaerere: 'flee to ask', i.e. avoid asking.

latin: quem Fors dierum cumque dabit, lucro
english: whatever of days Chance will give, to profit
note: quem ... cumque: tmesis of quemcumque, 'whichever (day)'. Fors: Chance personified.

english: set it down, and not sweet loves
note: lucro adpone: 'set down to profit', count as gain. nec negates sperne (line 16).

english: spurn, a boy, nor you the dances,
note: puer: 'being a boy', while you are a boy. neque tu (sperne) choreas: 'nor you spurn the dances'.

english: while from the green one white hair is absent,
note: virenti: dative, 'from you (who are) green', i.e. in your fresh youth.

latin: morosa. nunc et campus et areae
english: peevish. Now both the Campus and the squares
note: morosa agrees with canities (line 17). campus: the Campus Martius. areae: open spaces, courtyards.

english: and soft, towards night, whispers
at the appointed hour let be sought again,
note: repetantur: jussive subjunctive; subjects campus, areae, susurri.

english: now also, of the hiding one, the betrayer, from the inmost
note: latentis agrees with puellae (line 22): 'of the hiding girl'. intumo = intimo.

english: pleasing, of the girl, laughter, from the corner,
note: Construe: the pleasing laughter of the hiding girl, betrayer from the inmost corner.

english: and a pledge snatched from arms
note: lacertis: 'from (her) arms'; the pledge is a bracelet or ring taken from her.

english: or from a finger badly resisting.
note: male pertinaci: 'badly (i.e. scarcely) holding on', a finger that resists only feebly.

english: Mercurius, eloquent grandson of Atlas,
note: Mercuri: vocative of Mercurius.

audit.problem: Name anglicised: the vocative Mercuri is of Mercurius, while the batches otherwise keep Latin forms (Volcanus, Ulixes, Iuno); no note.

english: who the wild ways of men newly made
note: recentum = recentium: men newly created, primitive.

english: by speech shaped, clever, and of the comely
note: formasti = formavisti. decorae agrees with palaestrae (line 4).

english: by the custom of the wrestling-ground,
note: palaestra: the wrestling school; 'by the custom of the comely wrestling-school'.

latin: te canam, magni Iovis et deorum
english: you I shall sing, of great Jupiter and of the gods
the messenger, and of the curved lyre the parent,
clever, whatever has pleased you, in playful
note: iocoso agrees with furto (line 8): 'in playful theft'. placuit: 'has pleased (you)'.

english: to stow away, theft.
note: callidum ... condere: 'clever at stowing away'; furto: 'by (playful) theft'.

english: you, once, unless you had given back the cattle
note: te is object of risit (line 12): 'laughed at you'. Words of Apollo's threat reported indirectly.

english: by trickery removed, a boy, with threatening
note: amotas agrees with boves (line 9). puerum: you, then a boy. minaci agrees with voce (line 11).

english: voice while he frightens, bereft of his quiver,
note: viduus pharetra: 'widowed of (his) quiver'; Mercury had stolen it as well. 'his' supplied.

english: Apollo laughed.

latin: quin et Atridas duce te superbos
english: indeed also the Atridae, with you as guide, the proud
note: Atridae: the sons of Atreus

audit.problem: The patronymic Atridas is paraphrased as 'the sons of Atreus' instead of the name in the Latin (H01 keeps Pelides and Tydides).

english: Ilium left behind, rich Priam
note: Ilio relicto: ablative absolute.

english: and the Thessalian fires and, hostile to Troy,
note: iniqua agrees with castra (line 16): 'the camp hostile to Troy'.

english: the camp, eluded.
note: fefellit: 'escaped the notice of'; objects Atridas, ignis, castra.

english: you the pious souls in happy
note: laetis agrees with sedibus (line 18): 'in happy abodes'.

english: abodes lay to rest, and with a wand the light
note: levem agrees with turbam (line 19).

english: golden, the throng; to the upper of the gods
note: aurea agrees with virga (line 18): 'with golden wand'. superis deorum: 'to the gods above'.

english: pleasing, and to the lowest.
note: imis: 'to the lowest (gods)', those below.

latin: Tu ne quaesieris, scire nefas, quem mihi, quem tibi
english: You, do not ask — to know is unlawful — what for me, what for you
note: ne quaesieris: perfect subjunctive prohibition. quem (masculine) agrees with finem (line 2): 'what end for me, what for you'. nefas: forbidden by divine law.

latin: finem di dederint, Leuconoe, nec Babylonios
english: end the gods have given, Leuconoe, and not Babylonian
note: dederint: perfect subjunctive in indirect question.

latin: temptaris numeros. ut melius, quidquid erit, pati.
english: numbers try. How better, whatever will be, to endure!
note: temptaris = temptaveris, prohibition continued by nec. Babylonios numeros: astrological calculations. ut melius: exclamation.

latin: seu pluris hiemes seu tribuit Iuppiter ultimam,
english: whether more winters, or Jupiter has allotted as the last

latin: quae nunc oppositis debilitat pumicibus mare
english: the one which now on opposing pumice-stones weakens the sea
note: quae refers to the winter (hiemem understood with ultimam): the winter which wears out the sea against the rocks.

latin: Tyrrhenum: sapias, vina liques et spatio brevi
english: Tyrrhenian: be wise, strain the wines, and to a brief span
note: sapias, liques, reseces: subjunctives of exhortation. spatio brevi: 'because of the brief span', or 'to (fit) a brief span'.

latin: spem longam reseces. dum loquimur, fugerit invida
english: long hope cut back. While we speak, will have fled grudging
note: reseces: pruning metaphor, 'cut back' (like a vine); meaning: curtail far-reaching hopes. invida agrees with aetas (line 8).

latin: aetas: carpe diem quam minimum credula postero.
english: time: pluck the day, as little as possible trusting the next.
note: carpe diem: 'pluck the day' (metaphor of gathering fruit or flowers): make use of today. credula agrees with Leuconoe. postero: 'to the next (day)'.

latin: Quem virum aut heroa lyra vel acri
english: What man or hero, on the lyre or on the shrill
note: acri agrees with tibia (line 2).

english: pipe, do you take up to celebrate, Clio?
note: Clio: the Muse of history.

english: what god? whose will re-echo, playful,
note: iocosa agrees with imago (line 4): 'the playful image' will sing back.

english: name the image
note: imago: 'image', here the echo. Construe: whose name will the playful echo sing back.

english: either on the shady of Helicon borders
note: umbrosis agrees with oris: 'on the shady slopes of Helicon'.

latin: aut super Pindo gelidove in Haemo?
english: or upon Pindus, or on cold Haemus?
whence the vocal one, heedlessly having followed,
note: vocalem agrees with Orphea (line 8). insecutae agrees with silvae (line 8).

english: Orpheus, the woods,
note: Construe: whence (from Haemus) the woods followed tuneful Orpheus heedlessly.

english: by maternal art the swift delaying
note: arte materna: art from his mother, the Muse Calliope. rapidos agrees with lapsus (line 10). morantem agrees with Orphea.

english: glidings of rivers and the swift winds,
charming too the eared, with tuneful strings,
note: blandum: '(so) charming (as) to lead'. auritas agrees with quercus (line 12): oaks given ears. fidibus canoris: 'with tuneful strings'.

english: to lead, oaks.
What shall I say before the customary of the Parent
note: solitis agrees with laudibus (line 14): 'before the customary praises of the Parent' (Jupiter).

latin: laudibus, qui res hominum ac deorum,
english: praises, who the affairs of men and of gods,

latin: qui mare ac terras variisque mundum
english: who the sea and the lands and, with varied, the universe
note: variis agrees with horis (line 16).

english: governs, seasons?
note: temperat: 'regulates'. horis: 'with (varied) seasons'.

english: whence nothing greater is begotten than himself
note: ipso: ablative of comparison.

latin: nec viget quidquam simile aut secundum.
english: nor flourishes anything like or second.
the nearest to him, however, has seized
note: proximos agrees with honores (line 20).

english: Pallas, the honours,
in battles bold. Nor you shall I pass over in silence,
note: audax agrees with Pallas, as the source punctuates (stop after audax); some editors attach proeliis audax to Liber in line 22.

english: Liber, and, to savage hostile, maiden
note: Liber: Bacchus. inimica agrees with virgo: the maiden (Diana) hostile to savage beasts.

english: beasts, nor you, to be feared for the sure
note: metuende: vocative gerundive, 'you who are to be feared'. certa agrees with sagitta (line 24).

english: Phoebus, arrow.
note: certa sagitta: 'for (your) unerring arrow'.

english: I shall tell also of Alcides and the boys of Leda,
note: Alciden: Alcides, Hercules. pueros Ledae: Castor and Pollux.

english: this one with horses, that one at overcoming with fists
note: superare: infinitive with nobilem (line 27): 'famous for overcoming'.

english: famous; whose, as soon as, white to sailors,
note: quorum ... alba ... stella: 'whose white star'. simul = as soon as.

english: star has shone back,
note: refulsit: the star of the Dioscuri, St Elmo's fire, seen by sailors.

english: flows down from the rocks the stirred-up spray,
note: umor: 'moisture', the spray. Order: the stirred-up water flows down from the rocks.

english: the winds fall, and the clouds flee,

latin: et minax, quia sic voluere, ponto
english: and the threatening, because thus they willed, on the sea
note: minax agrees with unda (line 32). voluere: perfect (voluerunt), 'they' = the Dioscuri.

english: wave lies back down.

latin: Romulum post hos prius an quietum
english: Romulus after these first, or the quiet
note: Indirect questions depending on dubito (line 35): whether I should recall first Romulus or ...

english: reign of Pompilius shall I recall, or the proud
note: Pompili: Numa Pompilius. memorem: deliberative subjunctive.

english: rods of Tarquinius, I am in doubt, or of Cato
note: fascis: the fasces, rods of office; Tarquinius Superbus. Catonis: Cato of Utica.

english: the noble death:
Regulus and the Scauri and of his great soul
note: animae magnae prodigum: 'lavish of his great soul' (life). 'his' supplied.

english: prodigal Paulus, the Carthaginian prevailing,
note: superante Poeno: ablative absolute, at Cannae. Poeno: 'the Phoenician', Carthaginian (Hannibal).

english: grateful, with distinguished, I shall record, Camena,
note: insigni agrees with camena: 'with a distinguished Camena', i.e. in noble verse. Camena: Italian Muse.

english: and Fabricius.
him and, with unkempt, Curius, hair,
note: incomptis agrees with capillis: 'Curius with unkempt hair'.

english: useful in war, bore, and Camillus,
harsh poverty and an ancestral, with fitting
note: avitus agrees with fundus (line 44); apto agrees with lare.

english: with household god, farm.
note: apto cum lare: 'with a household (god) fitted to it', a homestead matching the farm. lar: the household god, metonymy for home.

english: grows, by hidden, like a tree, time
note: occulto agrees with aevo: 'in unseen lapse of time'.

english: the fame of Marcellus; gleams among all
note: Marcelli: of Marcellus (the conqueror of Syracuse, with allusion to the young Marcellus). Text doubtful: some editors emend to Marcellis (dative); source reading kept.

english: the Julian star, as among fires
note: Iulium sidus: the star of the Julian house (Caesar's comet). ignis: accusative plural.

english: the moon the lesser.
note: minores agrees with ignis (line 47): 'among the lesser fires'.

english: of the human race father and guardian,
sprung from Saturn, to you the care of great
note: orte Saturno: vocative participle, to Jupiter, son of Saturn.

english: Caesar by the fates has been given: you, with second
note: secundo Caesare: ablative absolute, 'with Caesar (as) second'.

english: Caesar, may you reign.
note: regnes: jussive or optative subjunctive.

english: he, whether the Parthians, over Latium looming,
note: imminentis: accusative plural agreeing with Parthos.

english: shall have driven, tamed, in a just triumph,
or, lying under the shores of the East,
note: subiectos agrees with Seras et Indos (line 56): those who lie under (bordering) the regions of the Orient. orae: dative.

english: the Seres and the Indians,
note: Seras: the Seres, the Chinese.

latin: te minor latum reget aequos orbem:
english: lesser than you, the broad will rule, just, world:
note: te minor: 'inferior to you'. latum agrees with orbem. aequos = aequus, nominative: he as a just ruler.

english: you with heavy chariot will shake Olympus,
you, on too-little chaste, hostile, will send
note: parum castis agrees with lucis (line 60): 'on unchaste groves'. inimica agrees with fulmina.

english: thunderbolts, groves.
note: fulmina inimica: 'hostile thunderbolts'. lucis: dative, 'onto the groves' (profaned groves).

english: When you, Lydia, Telephus's
note: Telephi: genitive of Telephus, with cervicem (line 2).

english: neck rosy, the waxen of Telephus
note: cerea agrees with bracchia (line 3): 'the waxen arms of Telephus'.

english: you praise, arms, alas, my
seething with difficult bile swells liver.
note: meum ... iecur: 'my liver' swells. difficili bile: 'with peevish bile'; the liver as seat of anger and passion.

latin: tum nec mens mihi nec color
english: then neither mind for me nor colour

latin: certa sede manet, umor et in genas
english: in fixed seat remains, and moisture onto the cheeks
note: certa sede: 'in a sure place'. umor: a tear.

english: stealthily glides, proving
note: arguens: 'proving', showing.

english: how by slow, deep within, I am steeped, fires.
note: lentis agrees with ignibus: 'with slow fires'. macerer: 'I am soaked, wasted'; metaphor of steeping, meaning consumed.

english: I burn, whether for you the white
have fouled shoulders, immoderate in unmixed wine,
note: turparunt = turpaverunt. inmodicae agrees with rixae (line 11). mero: 'with unmixed wine'.

english: brawls, or a boy raging
has pressed a remembering, with his tooth, on the lips, mark.
note: memorem agrees with notam: 'a mark that remembers', a lasting mark. 'his' supplied; labris: 'on (your) lips'.

english: Not, if me enough you were to hear,
note: non goes with speres (line 14): 'you would not hope'.

english: would you hope lasting, the sweet barbarously
note: perpetuum: '(him) lasting', Telephus as constant; 'him' understood. dulcia agrees with oscula (line 15).

english: harming, kisses, which Venus
note: laedentem agrees with the understood 'him': 'one who barbarously hurts the sweet kisses'.

english: with the fifth part of her nectar has steeped.
note: quinta parte: the quintessence, the finest part. sui: 'of her own' nectar.

english: happy thrice and more

latin: quos inrupta tenet copula nec malis
english: whom an unbroken holds bond, and not by bad
note: inrupta agrees with copula: 'an unbroken bond'. nec negates solvet (line 20). malis agrees with querimoniis (line 19).

english: torn apart, complaints,
note: divolsus agrees with amor (line 20): 'love torn apart by bad complaints'.

english: sooner than the last will love release, day.
note: suprema ... die: 'than the last day'. solvet: 'will release (them)'.

latin: O navis, referent in mare te novi
english: O ship, will carry back to sea you new
note: novi agrees with fluctus (line 2). The ship is commonly read as an allegory of the state.

latin: fluctus. o quid agis? fortiter occupa
english: waves. Oh, what are you doing? Bravely seize
the harbour. Do you not see how
bare of oarage the side
note: nudum agrees with latus: 'the side bare of oars'; the verb is supplied from gemant (line 6).

english: and the mast, by swift wounded Africus,
note: celeri agrees with Africo: 'wounded by the swift Africus' (the south-west wind).

english: and the yards groan, and without ropes
note: gemant: subjunctive in indirect question after vides ut. funibus: undergirding cables.

english: scarcely to endure the keels
are able the more imperious
note: imperiosius agrees with aequor (line 9): 'the too imperious sea'. carinae: plural for the hull.

latin: aequor? non tibi sunt integra lintea,
english: sea? Not for you are whole sails,
note: lintea: 'linen', sails.

latin: non di, quos iterum pressa voces malo.
english: not gods, whom again, pressed, you might call on, by evil.
note: di: images of the gods on the stern, lost. pressa agrees with the ship: 'pressed by evil'. voces: subjunctive.

english: although, Pontic pine,
note: Pontica pinus: vocative, the ship built of Pontic pine.

english: of a forest the daughter noble,

latin: iactes et genus et nomen inutile:
english: you boast both lineage and name useless:
nothing, in painted, the timid sailor, sterns
note: nil ... fidit: 'trusts not at all'. pictis agrees with puppibus: 'in painted sterns'.

english: trusts. You, unless to the winds
note: nisi ... debes ludibrium: 'unless you owe the winds a mockery'.

english: you owe a plaything, beware.
note: ludibrium: 'a plaything, mockery'; meaning: unless you are fated to be the sport of the winds.

english: lately anxious which to me weariness,
note: quae: 'you who'. sollicitum taedium: 'an anxious weariness', a cause of disgust. mihi: 'to me'.

english: now longing and care not light,
poured between the shining
note: interfusa agrees with aequora (line 20): seas poured between. nitentis agrees with Cycladas.

english: may you avoid seas, Cyclades.
note: vites: subjunctive of wish. Cycladas: accusative, Greek form; the Cyclades islands.

latin: Pastor cum traheret per freta navibus
english: When the shepherd was dragging across the straits in ships
note: Pastor: Paris, the shepherd of Ida.

english: Idaean Helen, the faithless one, his hostess,
note: Idaeis agrees with navibus: 'Idaean ships' (built of timber from Ida). perfidus agrees with pastor. hospitam: Helen, wife of his host. 'his' supplied.

english: in unwelcome the swift overwhelmed calm
note: ingrato agrees with otio: 'in an unwelcome calm'. celeres agrees with ventos (line 4). Subject: Nereus (line 5).

english: winds, that he might sing the fierce
Nereus fates. "With evil you lead omen home
note: fera agrees with fata. mala ... avi: 'with an evil bird', bad omen. Quotation marks as in the source: Nereus' prophecy begins here and runs to the end of the poem.

english: whom with much will seek again Greece soldiery
note: quam: Helen (feminine). multo agrees with milite: 'with many a soldier' (collective singular); Graecia is subject.

english: sworn together to break your nuptials
note: coniurata agrees with Graecia.

english: and the kingdom of Priam old.

latin: heu heu, quantus equis, quantus adest viris
english: alas, alas, how much for horses, how much is at hand for men
note: quantus agrees with sudor (line 10).

english: sweat, how many you set in motion funerals for the Dardanian
note: Dardanae agrees with genti (line 11).

latin: genti. iam galeam Pallas et aegida
english: race. Already the helmet Pallas and the aegis
note: aegida: Greek accusative of aegis, Pallas' shield.

english: and the chariot and the rage prepares.
In vain, on Venus' protection fierce,
you will comb your hair and, pleasing to women,
note: caesariem: 'the long hair'. 'your' supplied. grata agrees with carmina (line 15).

english: on the unwarlike lyre songs you will divide;
note: divides: 'you will apportion', sing in parts, measures.

english: in vain in the bedchamber the heavy
note: gravis agrees with hastas (line 17).

english: spears and of the reed the points Cnosian
note: calami spicula: 'the points of the reed', arrows. Cnosii agrees with calami: Cretan (Cnossian) reed.

english: you will avoid, and the din, and swift to pursue
note: celerem sequi: 'swift to pursue', with Aiacem.

english: Aiax: nevertheless, alas, late, adulterous
note: serus: 'late', though late. adulteros agrees with crines (line 20).

audit.problem: Name anglicised: Aiacem is Aiax in the Latin form the batches otherwise keep (Ulixes); no note.

english: hair with dust you will defile.
note: collines: 'you will smear'; dust of death.

english: Not Laertiades, ruin of your
note: Laertiades: the son of Laertes, Ulixes

audit.problem: The patronymic Laertiaden is paraphrased as 'the son of Laertes' instead of the name in the Latin (H01 keeps Pelides, Tydides).

english: race, not Pylian Nestor, do you look back at?
note: respicis: 'do you regard', see behind you.

english: press, fearless, you, Salaminian
note: urgent: subjects Teucer, Sthenelus. inpavidi: nominative plural.

english: Teucer, you Sthenelus, skilled
note: sciens: 'knowing', skilled, with pugnae (line 25).

latin: pugnae sive opus est imperitare equis,
english: of fight, or, if there is need to command horses,
note: sive: 'or, if' (sive ... opus est).

english: no charioteer sluggish. Meriones also
note: non auriga piger: 'not a sluggish charioteer'.

latin: nosces. ecce furit, te reperire atrox,
english: you will come to know. Look, he rages to find you, fierce,
note: te reperire: 'to find you'. atrox agrees with Tydides.

english: Tydides, better than the father:
note: Tydides: Diomedes, son of Tydeus

audit.problem: Tydides is paraphrased as 'the son of Tydeus', whereas H01 (1.6.16) keeps 'Tydides'; inconsistent with the names rule.

latin: quem tu, cervus uti vallis in altera
english: whom you, as a stag, of a valley in the other
note: uti = ut. altera agrees with parte (line 30): 'in the other part of the valley'.

english: seen part, a wolf, of the grass unmindful,
note: visum agrees with lupum: 'a wolf seen'. inmemor: 'forgetful of the grass' (the stag).

english: with high you will flee, soft, panting,
note: sublimi anhelitu: 'with high (deep, upheaved) panting'. mollis: 'soft one', effeminate.

english: not this having promised your.
note: tuae: 'to your (woman)', Helen. pollicitus: 'having promised'.

english: the angry will postpone the day for Ilium
note: iracunda agrees with classis (line 34): 'the wrathful fleet'.

english: and for the matrons of the Phrygians, fleet of Achilles;
note: Achillei: genitive of Achilles.

english: after fixed winters will burn Achaean
note: certas hiemes: 'a fixed number of winters'. Achaicus agrees with ignis (line 36).

english: fire Ilian houses.
note: Closing quotation mark absent in source; Nereus' speech ends here.

english: O daughter more beautiful than a beautiful mother,
note: matre pulcra: ablative of comparison.

english: whatever, to the abusive, you will wish, limit
note: quem ... cumque: tmesis of quemcumque, agreeing with modum; criminosis agrees with iambis on line 3: abusive iambics.

audit.problem: criminosis is an adjective agreeing with iambis ('abusive'), but the line renders it as a purpose phrase 'for accusing'.

latin: tu, cum parentis regna per arduum
english: You, when, of your father, the realms, by the steep,
note: parentis: Jupiter; 'your' supplied. per arduum: up the steep way.

english: the band of Giants was climbing, impious,
note: scanderet: imperfect subjunctive with cum; inpia agrees with cohors.

english: Rhoetus you hurled back, with the lion's
note: Rhoetus: one of the Giants. Bacchus fought in lion form.

english: claws and dreadful jaw;
note: mala: ablative singular of mala, jaw.

english: although for dances fitter and jests
and play said, not enough suited
note: dictus: having been called; non sat: 'not enough', negative kept.

english: for fight, you were reputed; but the same
note: ferebaris: you were said, reputed. idem: the same (you).

english: of peace you were, and the middle, of war.
note: medius: the mid-point, i.e. you were the same (you) both in peace and in the midst of war; pacis and belli both depend on medius.

english: Cerberus, harmless, saw you, with golden
note: te is object, Cerberus subject: Cerberus saw you. insons: unharming, innocent (made gentle).

english: horn adorned, gently rubbing
note: decorum agrees with te: you adorned with the golden horn. atterens: rubbing (against you) his tail.

english: his tail, and, departing, with three-tongued
note: recedentis: genitive, 'of (you) departing', with pedes (line 32). 'his' supplied.

english: mouth the feet, and touched the legs.
note: pedes ... crura: your feet and legs (licked them).

english: Not on an ordinary nor a slender shall I be borne
note: non ... nec: negatives kept in place. ferar: future passive.

english: wing, two-formed, through the liquid air
note: penna: wing (lit. feather). biformis: of two forms, man and bird (also poet). aethera: Greek accusative, the upper air.

english: bard, nor on the earth shall I delay
note: vates: poet-prophet.

english: longer, and, than envy greater,
note: invidia: ablative of comparison.

english: cities shall I leave. Not I, of poor
note: urbis = urbes, accusative plural.

latin: sanguis parentum, non ego, quem vocas.
english: blood of parents, not I, whom you call.
note: sanguis: offspring. quem vocas: 'whom you call (to you)', or 'whom you call (dear)'; Shorey's text has a full stop here, which is kept, but the sense runs on into the vocative of line 7.

english: beloved Maecenas, shall die
note: obibo: shall go to death, perish.

english: nor by the Stygian wave shall I be held.
note: Stygia ... unda: by the wave of the Styx.

english: Already, already settle on my legs rough
note: residunt: settle, sink in. cruribus: dative/ablative, 'on the shins'; 'my' supplied.

latin: pelles et album mutor in alitem
english: skins, and into a white I am changed bird
note: album ... alitem: a white bird (the swan).

english: above, and there spring up smooth
note: superne: on the upper parts.

english: over fingers and shoulders feathers.
Already, than Daedalean Icarus better known,
note: notior: Shorey's reading; many editors read ocior, 'swifter'. Daedaleo: son of Daedalus.

english: I shall visit the shores of groaning Bosporus
note: gementis ... Bospori: 'of the groaning Bosporus'.

english: and the Gaetulian Syrtes, tuneful
note: Syrtis = Syrtes, the shoals off North Africa; Gaetulian = African.

english: bird, and Hyperborean plains.
note: Hyperboreos: of the far North.

latin: me Colchus et qui dissimulat metum
english: Me the Colchian, and who hides fear
note: qui dissimulat metum: the Dacian who hides (pretends not to have) fear.

english: of the Marsian cohort, the Dacian, and the farthest
note: Marsae cohortis: the Marsian troops, the best Roman infantry.

english: Geloni shall know; me the skilled
note: Geloni: Scythian tribe.

english: shall learn, the Iberian, and of the Rhone the drinker.
note: peritus Hiber: the learned Spaniard; Rhodani potor: the Gaul.

english: Let be absent from my empty funeral dirges
note: inani funere: the funeral is empty (there is no body); 'my' supplied. neniae: dirges.

english: and unseemly mournings and laments;
check the outcry, and of the tomb
omit the superfluous honours.
note: mitte: let go, omit.

english: I hate the uninitiated crowd and keep it off.
note: profanum: outside the shrine, uninitiated. arceo: keep away; 'it' supplied.

english: Be favourable with tongues: songs not before
note: favete linguis: ritual formula, 'speak words of good omen', i.e. keep holy silence.

english: heard, of the Muses the priest,
for maidens and boys I sing.
Of kings to be feared over their own flocks
note: Sense: the command of dreaded kings is over their own flocks (the verb est is in line 6); 'their' renders proprios.

latin: reges in ipsos imperium est Iovis,
english: over kings themselves the command is of Jove,
note: Iovis: of Jupiter.

english: famous for the Giant triumph,
note: Giganteo triumpho: the triumph over the Giants.

english: all things with an eyebrow moving.
note: supercilio: by his brow (nod).

latin: est ut viro vir latius ordinet
english: It is (so) that man than man more widely arranges
note: est ut: it may be that. viro: dative/ablative of comparison 'than (another) man'.

english: plantations in furrows, this one more nobly born
note: arbusta: tree-plantings (trees for training vines). sulcis: in furrows (trenches).

english: goes down into the Field as candidate,
note: campum: the Campus Martius, where elections were held. descendat: subjunctive after est ut.

english: in morals this one and better in repute
note: moribus ... fama: ablative of respect.

english: contends, for that one the crowd of clients
note: contendat: subjunctive (after est ut). illi: dative.

english: is greater: by equal law Necessity
note: sit: subjunctive. Necessitas: personified.

english: allots the distinguished and the lowest;
note: sortitur: draws lots for, assigns by lot; insignis = insignes.

english: the roomy urn shakes every name.
note: omne ... nomen is object, urna subject: the capacious urn shakes every name (lots in the urn).

english: Drawn sword for whom above the impious
note: cui: the man over whose impious neck the drawn sword hangs (Damocles). destrictus: unsheathed.

english: neck hangs, not Sicilian feasts
note: Siculae dapes: the proverbial luxury of the Syracusan tyrants.

english: a sweet flavour will work out,
note: elaborabunt: will produce with effort.

english: not of birds and of the lyre the singing
note: avium: of birds (in aviaries).

english: sleep will bring back: sleep, of rustic
note: Negatives in lines 18 and 20 kept in place.

english: gentle, men, not humble houses
note: agrestium ... virorum: of countrymen; non humilis domos: not the humble houses (it does not disdain them).

english: disdains, and the shady bank,
note: fastidit: disdains; non (line 22, line 24) negates it.

english: not Tempe stirred by Zephyrs.
note: Tempe: Greek neuter plural, the valley in Thessaly; Zephyris: by west winds. 'not' repeats from line 22: (does not disdain) Tempe.

english: The one desiring what is enough neither
note: desiderantem: accusative, object of sollicitat (line 26).

english: does the tumultuous sea trouble
note: sollicitat: troubles, disturbs; subject mare.

english: nor the savage, of Arcturus setting,
note: Arcturi cadentis: the setting of Arcturus (late October), stormy season.

english: onset, or of the rising Kid,
note: Haedi: the Kid, a star rising in early October, also a storm-sign.

english: not lashed by hail vineyards
and the farm, lying, the tree now the waters
note: fundus mendax: a deceitful farm (failing its promise). arbore: ablative absolute with culpante (line 31), 'the tree blaming'.

english: blaming, now scorching the fields
note: torrentia agros: torrentia is the participle agreeing with sidera (line 32).

english: stars, now winters unfair.
note: Construction (lines 29-32): the troubles listed do not trouble (sollicitat, line 26) the man content with enough.

english: The fish feel the waters narrowed
note: The fish (subject) feel the waters (object) narrowed.

latin: iactis in altum molibus: huc frequens
english: by masses thrown into the deep: hither thronging
note: molibus: masses, piles (foundations of seaside villas). frequens: in numbers, with a crowd.

english: rubble lets down the contractor
note: caementa: rough stones for concrete. redemptor: the building contractor.

english: with servants, and the master, of land
note: terrae ... fastidiosus: weary of (scorning) land.

english: disdainful: but Fear and Threats
note: Timor, Minae: personified.

english: climb to the same place where the master (does), nor
note: eodem, quo: to the same place to which.

english: withdraws from the bronze-beaked trireme, and
note: aerata: bronze-fitted (beaked).

english: behind the horseman sits black Care.
note: Cura: Care, personified.

english: But if the one grieving neither Phrygian stone
note: Phrygius lapis: Phrygian (Synnadic) marble. dolentem: object of delenit (line 43).

english: nor, of purples than a star brighter,
note: purpurarum ... usus: the use (wearing) of purple garments brighter than a star.

english: soothes, the use, nor Falernian
vine and Achaemenian costus,
note: Achaemenium: Persian. costum: costus, an aromatic perfume (unguent).

english: why, with doorposts to be envied and in new
note: invidendis: gerundive, to be envied.

english: lofty fashion should I build up an atrium?
note: sublime: lofty, agreeing with atrium. moliar: deliberative subjunctive.

english: Why for the valley should I exchange Sabine
note: valle ... Sabina: ablative of exchange, for my Sabine valley.

english: riches more laborious?
note: operosiores: more troublesome (requiring more toil).

english: Narrow, as a friend, poverty to endure
note: amice: adverb, in friendly fashion (gladly). Some editors read amici; Shorey prints amice.

english: sturdy, in harsh soldiering, a boy
note: militia: ablative, in military service.

english: let learn thoroughly, and the Parthians fierce
note: condiscat: jussive subjunctive. ferocis = feroces.

english: let him harass, a horseman to be feared with spear,
note: vexet: jussive. metuendus: gerundive.

latin: vitamque sub divo et trepidis agat
english: and life under the open sky and in anxious let him spend
note: sub divo: under the sky, in the open air. trepidis ... in rebus: amid dangers.

latin: in rebus. illum ex moenibus hosticis
english: affairs. Him from the walls of the enemy
note: hosticis: hostile, of the enemy.

english: the matron of the warring tyrant
note: matrona: the wife of the enemy king.

english: looking out, and the grown maiden,
note: adulta virgo: the marriageable daughter.

english: may sigh: "alas, lest the unskilled in battle-lines
note: Quotation marks as in the Latin source. ne ... lacessat: 'lest (he) provoke' (fear clause). rudis agminum: unpractised in battle-columns.

english: betrothed provoke, royal, the rough
note: sponsus regius: the royal betrothed.

english: to touch, lion, whom bloody
note: asperum tactu: rough to touch (dangerous to handle); leonem: the Roman youth as lion.

english: through the midst of slaughters sweeps wrath."
note: rapit: snatches, carries headlong. Closing quotation mark as in the Latin source.

latin: dulce et decorum est pro patria mori:
english: Sweet and fitting it is for fatherland to die:
note: decorum: seemly, fitting.

english: death also pursues the fleeing man
note: mors (subject) pursues the fleeing man (object): fugacem ... virum.

english: nor spares, of unwarlike youth,
note: inbellis iuventae: genitive with poplitibus (line 16).

english: the hamstrings and the timid back.
note: poplitibus: the backs of the knees (dative with parcit).

english: Virtue, of defeat ignorant, sordid,
note: repulsae ... sordidae: of base electoral rebuff (repulsa = defeat at the polls); Virtus: personified.

english: with unstained honours shines
note: intaminatis ... honoribus: with untainted offices (honours).

english: nor takes up or lays down the axes
note: securis = secures, the axes of the fasces, emblems of office.

english: at the decision of the popular breeze.
note: aurae: breeze, i.e. popular favour.

english: Virtue, opening to the undeserving to die
note: inmeritis mori: to those not deserving to die.

english: heaven, by a denied way tries a journey,
note: negata ... via: by a way refused (to others).

english: and gatherings common and the damp
note: coetus: assemblies, crowds.

english: spurns the ground with fleeing wing.
note: penna: wing (lit. feather).

english: There is also for faithful, safe, silence
note: fideli ... silentio: for loyal silence; tuta: safe, agreeing with merces.

english: a reward: I shall forbid that he who, of Ceres, the rite
note: vetabo ... sit / solvat: I shall forbid that he be / unmoor. Cereris sacrum: the mysteries of Ceres (Eleusinian).

english: has divulged, secret, under the same
note: volgarit = volgaverit, perfect subjunctive. arcanae agrees with Cereris: 'of secret Ceres'.

english: be beams, and the fragile with me
note: trabibus: roof-beams; sit: subjunctive after vetabo.

english: unmoor the bean-boat; often Diespiter,
note: phaselon: Greek accusative of phaselus, a light boat (lit. 'bean-pod'). Diespiter: Jupiter (old form).

english: neglected, to the impure has added the pure;
note: incesto ... integrum: has joined the innocent with the guilty (in punishment).

english: rarely the one going ahead, wicked,
note: antecedentem scelestum: the criminal running ahead.

english: has abandoned, with foot, Punishment, lame.
note: pede ... claudo: with lame foot; Poena: Punishment, personified. addidit, deseruit: gnomic perfects.

english: The just man, and tenacious of his purpose,
note: virum is object of quatit (line 4); propositi: genitive with tenacem, 'of resolve'; 'his' supplied.

english: not the ardour of citizens ordering crooked things,
note: prava iubentium: urging (commanding) wrong, lit. crooked, things. non ... non ... neque ... nec (lines 2-6) kept where they stand.

english: not the face of a pressing tyrant
note: voltus: countenance; instantis: pressing, menacing.

english: shakes in his solid mind, nor Auster,
note: mente ... solida: ablative, 'in (from) his firm mind'; 'his' supplied. Auster: the south wind.

english: the turbulent leader of the restless Hadria,
note: Hadria (masc.): the Adriatic sea; the south wind as its 'leader', i.e. its master who stirs it.

english: nor the great hand of lightning-hurling Jove:
if, broken, the round world should slip down upon him,
note: orbis: the round, the world (or vault of heaven); inlabatur: present subjunctive, 'should fall in (upon him)'; 'upon him' renders the prefix in-.

english: the ruins will strike him unafraid.
note: inpavidum: accusative, him (the just man) unafraid.

latin: hac arte Pollux et vagus Hercules
english: By this art Pollux and wandering Hercules,
note: hac arte: by this quality (steadfastness), lit. art.

english: having striven upward, reached the fiery citadels,
note: enisus: having struggled up; attigit singular with the nearer subject; arcis igneas: the fiery heights of heaven (the stars).

english: among whom Augustus, reclining,
note: quos inter: anastrophe, 'between whom'.

english: with purple mouth will drink nectar;
note: bibet (Shorey), future; variant bibit noted. purpureo: purple, i.e. glowing (with divine youth).

latin: hac te merentem, Bacche pater, tuae
english: by this you, deserving, Bacchus father, your
note: hac (arte): by this (quality).

english: tigers carried, the yoke with untaught
note: vexere: perfect, 'carried'; iugum is object of trahentes (line 15); indocili collo: on an unteachable neck.

english: neck drawing; by this Quirinus
note: Quirinus: the deified Romulus.

english: on the horses of Mars fled Acheron,
note: Acheronta: Greek accusative; fugit: perfect, 'escaped' the river of the dead.

english: a pleasing thing having spoken out to the deliberating
note: gratum elocuta ... Iunone (line 18): ablative absolute, 'Juno having spoken (something) welcome'.

english: Juno, to the gods: “Ilion, Ilion
note: Quotation marks as in the source text: Juno's speech runs to line 68.

english: a fateful and unchaste judge
note: fatalis incestusque iudex: Paris, the judge of the goddesses.

english: and a foreign woman has turned
note: mulier peregrina: Helen; vertit: perfect, singular with the nearer subject, 'has overturned'.

latin: in pulverem ex quo destituit deos
english: into dust, from the time when defrauded the gods
note: ex quo: since; destituit: left in the lurch, cheated; subject Laomedon (line 22).

english: of the bargained wage Laomedon, to me
note: mercede pacta: ablative, of the agreed pay (for building Troy's walls); mihi: dative of agent with damnatum.

english: and to chaste Minerva condemned,
note: damnatum agrees with Ilion (line 18).

english: with its people and its deceitful leader.
note: 'its' supplied (twice); duce fraudulento: Laomedon.

english: Now neither for the Laconian adulteress gleams
note: Lacaenae ... adulterae: dative, the Spartan woman, Helen; nec ... nec (lines 25-26) kept in place.

english: the infamous guest, nor the house of Priam
note: famosus hospes: Paris; splendet: gleams (in finery).

english: perjured the combative Achivi
note: periura agrees with domus; Achivos (the Achaeans) is object of refringit.

english: with Hectorean resources breaks back,
note: Hectoreis opibus: with Hector's might (power); refringit: breaks, beats back.

english: and, by our dissensions drawn out,
note: nostris seditionibus: the gods' own quarrels; ductum: prolonged, agrees with bellum.

english: the war has settled down; forthwith both the heavy
note: resedit: perfect, has subsided; et ... et: both ... and.

english: angers and the hated grandson,
note: nepotem: Romulus, son of Mars (Juno's son) and Ilia.

english: whom the Trojan priestess bore,
note: Troica sacerdos: Ilia (Rhea Silvia), descended from Aeneas.

english: to Mars I shall give up; him I to the shining
note: redonabo: I shall give back (remit, forgive for Mars's sake).

english: seats to enter, to learn of nectar
note: lucidas ... sedes: the bright seats (of heaven).

english: the juices, and to be enrolled in the tranquil
note: sucos: juices, i.e. the drink; adscribi: be enrolled (as a citizen).

english: ranks of the gods I shall allow.
note: patiar: future, 'I shall suffer (allow)'.

english: As long as, long, between should rage Ilion
note: dum ... saeviat: present subjunctive; longus ... pontus: a long sea between Ilion and Rome.

english: and Rome the sea, in whatever, as exiles,
note: qualibet ... in parte: in any part whatever; exsules: as exiles.

english: part let them reign, blessed;
note: regnanto: future imperative, 3rd plural; subject the descendants of Troy (the Romans).

english: while on the tomb of Priam and of Paris
note: busto: dative with insultet.

english: should prance the herd, and the wild beasts their cubs
note: insultet: leap on, trample (in scorn); ferae (subject) and catulos (object) set in English order within the line.

english: should hide unpunished, let the Capitol stand
note: inultae: unpunished, with impunity; stet: jussive subjunctive.

english: gleaming, and, on the triumphed-over, may
note: triumphatis ... Medis (line 44): dative, the Medes led in triumph; possit: may (be able).

english: Rome fierce give laws, to the Medes.
note: dare iura: give laws (impose terms).

english: Dreadful far and wide, her name to the farthest
note: horrenda: nominative, agrees with Roma; 'her' supplied.

english: let her extend shores, where the middle liquid
note: in ultimas ... oras (lines 45-46): to the farthest shores; medius liquor: the intervening water (the Mediterranean, the straits).

english: separates Europe from the African,
note: Europen: Greek accusative; Afro: the African (man or land), i.e. Africa.

english: where the swollen Nile waters the fields.
note: rigat: waters, irrigates (with the flood).

latin: aurum inrepertum et sic melius situm,
english: Gold undiscovered and so better placed
note: inrepertum: not found; situm: laid, placed.

english: when the earth hides it, braver at spurning
note: fortior (Roma): stronger, braver to spurn; 'it' supplied.

english: than at gathering into human uses
note: cogere: to collect, force together.

english: with a right hand seizing everything sacred,
note: omne sacrum rapiente dextra: ablative absolute, plundering all that is holy.

english: whatever limit has stood in the world's way,
note: mundo: dative, 'has stood against the world'; obstitit: perfect.

english: this she will touch with arms, eager to visit
note: tanget: future; gestiens: longing, eager.

english: in which part fires may rage like Bacchants,
note: qua parte: in what region; debacchentur: subjunctive, rave in Bacchic frenzy (metaphor: the torrid zone).

english: in which clouds and rainy dews.
note: Verb understood from line 55; the clouds and rains of the frozen north.

english: But to the warlike Quirites the fates
note: Quiritibus: the Roman citizens.

latin: hac lege dico, ne nimium pii
english: on this condition I declare, lest, too much dutiful
note: hac lege: by this law, condition; ne: lest (negative purpose), kept where it stands; pii: devoted, dutiful (to Troy).

english: and trusting in their fortunes, of ancestral
note: rebus: circumstances, prosperity; avitae ... Troiae: of their grandfathers' Troy.

english: roofs they should wish to restore, of Troy.
note: Troiae: genitive with tecta and avitae on line 59

audit.problem: Troiae (genitive, with avitae on line 59 and tecta) is rendered as a bare 'Troy', so the line reads as if Troy were a separate noun; the 'of' was used up on line 59. Sense recoverable from the note.

english: Of Troy, reborn under a mournful bird,
note: alite lugubri: with a bird of ill omen (augury).

english: the fortune with sad slaughter shall be repeated,
note: fortuna Troiae renascens (line 61); iterabitur: future passive.

english: leading the victorious bands
note: ducente ... me (line 64): ablative absolute, 'I leading'.

english: I, wife of Jove and sister.
note: coniuge me Iovis et sorore: ablative absolute, me being the wife and sister of Jove.

english: Thrice if should rise again the bronze wall
note: resurgat ... pereat ... ploret: present subjunctives, future less vivid condition.

english: with Phoebus as founder, thrice would it perish, by my
note: auctore Phoebo: ablative absolute, with Phoebus (Apollo) as builder.

english: Argives cut down, thrice would the wife,
note: excisus: razed, cut down; meis Argivis: my Argives, the Greeks.

english: captured, her husband and boys bewail.”
note: virum: her husband; 'her' supplied. Closing quotation mark as in the source.

english: This will not suit a jesting lyre —
note: conveniet: future.

english: whither, Muse, are you heading? Cease, wilful one,
note: tendis: you are straining, going; pervicax: obstinate, vocative.

english: to report the talk of the gods and
note: sermones: conversations, discourses.

english: great things with small measures to make thin.
note: modis: measures, strains; tenuare: to thin, diminish.

latin: Descende caelo et dic age tibia
english: Come down from the sky and speak, come, on the pipe,
note: age: come! (imperative interjection); tibia: ablative, with (on) the reed pipe.

english: queen Calliope, a long melody,
note: regina: vocative; melos: Greek neuter, song, melody.

english: whether with voice now you prefer high,
note: voce ... acuta: with a high, clear voice.

english: or with strings or the cithara of Phoebus.
note: fidibus: lyre strings; citharave: or the cithara (lyre).

english: Do you hear? Or does there mock me a lovable
note: auditis: plural, addressed to the company; ludit: mocks, deceives.

english: madness? I seem both to hear and, holy,
note: audire et videor ... errare: 'I seem to hear and to wander'; pios ... lucos: sacred groves.

english: to wander through groves, which pleasant
note: amoenae agrees with aquae et aurae (line 8).

latin: quos et aquae subeunt et aurae.
english: both waters and breezes come beneath.
note: quos ... subeunt: steal into (pass under) the groves.

english: Me, the fabled ones, on Vultur in Apulia,
note: fabulosae: nominative plural with palumbes (line 12), storied, legendary; Volture: Mount Vultur.

english: outside the threshold of the nurse Pullia
note: Text doubtful: Pulliae (Shorey) is a conjecture; the manuscripts repeat Apuliae (after Apulo), which gives a metrical anomaly. Rendered as the source reads.

english: with play and wearied with sleep
note: ludo fatigatumque somno: wearied by play and by sleep.

english: with fresh foliage, a boy, the wood-doves
note: puerum: me as a boy; palumbes: subject of texere.

english: covered, a wonder which would be to all
note: texere: perfect, 'covered'; mirum quod foret: a marvel to be to all.

english: whoever of lofty Acerontia the nest
note: Aceruntia (Acherontia): a hill town in Apulia/Lucania, perched like a nest.

english: and the Bantine glades and the field
note: saltus Bantinos: the woodland pastures of Bantia.

english: rich hold, of low-lying Forentum,
note: humilis Forenti: of low Forentum; 'hold' = inhabit.

latin: ut tuto ab atris corpore viperis
english: how, with body safe from black vipers
note: ut: how, that; tuto ... corpore: ablative absolute, 'with my body safe'.

latin: dormirem et ursis, ut premerer sacra
